Under identical cooling conditions, two liquids that fall through the same temperature interval lose heat in proportion to their heat capacities. The one with the larger heat capacity takes longer. The times therefore replace the rates, and the unknown specific heat is read from the two masses, the known specific heat and the two times.
The working relations are m1 c1 / t1 = m2 c2 / t2 for the same temperature range and c2 = m1 c1 t2 / (m2 t1). Name each symbol, convert the data into SI units, and only then substitute.
Derive c2 = m1 c1 t2 / (m2 t1) from equal rates of heat loss over the same temperature interval. Identical conditions give m1 c1 (Δθ/t1) = m2 c2 (Δθ/t2). Δθ is the same and cancels.

exercises.question: Derive c2 = m1 c1 t2 / (m2 t1) from equal rates of heat loss over the same temperature interval.
steps: Identical conditions give m1 c1 (Δθ/t1) = m2 c2 (Δθ/t2).
Δθ is the same and cancels.
The surface, the room and the temperature interval must match, or the cancellation is not valid.

summary: Equal heat-loss rates over the same temperature interval give m1 c1 / t1 = m2 c2 / t2. The unknown specific heat is m1 c1 t2 / (m2 t1). The interval, the surface and the room have to match.
